loadtest.note: SpeedHQ is the codec inside full-bandwidth NDI; OMT's VMX is the same class but not identical. vMix/OBS compositing load is NOT included — treat results as a lower bound.

verdict.headline: Weakest link: Internet connection type (Wi-Fi; needs wired) - Plug the PC into the venue network with an Ethernet cable and turn Wi-Fi off. (+4 more blocking problem(s))

checks.title: France reachable
checks.detail: Answered: Orange (FR ISP), Free (FR ISP), Moji (Paris DC), MilkyWan (Paris DC), Scaleway (Paris DC), Bouygues (Paris), AWS eu-west-3 (Paris), Twitch ingest Paris.

checks.title: Round-trip time to France (p95)
checks.detail: Median of the p95 values of 8 France targets; they range from 225 ms (Orange (FR ISP)) to 1281 ms (AWS eu-west-3 (Paris)). The SRT latency below is computed from this; re-run with -SrtHost <partner IP> for the exact path.

checks.title: Round-trip stability (p99 - p50)
checks.detail: Worst spread between the typical (p50) and slowest 1 % (p99) ping: Moji (Paris DC). Big spread means jitter that SRT must absorb.

checks.title: Ping loss to France
checks.detail: Pooled over 5 target(s): 1 of 150 pings lost. Ignores ping (not a fault): Bouygues (Paris), AWS eu-west-3 (Paris), Twitch ingest Paris.

checks.title: UDP loss at SRT bitrate
checks.detail: Receiver-side loss over 3 iperf3 test(s) at 12.5 Mbps for 20 s each: iperf3.moji.fr 0.00 %, speedtest.milkywan.fr 0.00 %, ping.online.net 0.00 %.

checks.title: UDP loss bursts
checks.detail: No 1 s interval lost more than 5 % of its packets.

checks.title: Upload capacity vs. show needs
checks.detail: Measured upload to a nearby Cloudflare PoP: 81.6 Mbps. The show needs 36.0 Mbps (SRT video+audio with 25 % overhead, YouTube, Twitch), ratio 2.3 x.

checks.title: Internet connection type
checks.detail: The default route (internet) goes through the Wi-Fi adapter WiFi.
checks.fix: Plug the PC into the venue network with an Ethernet cable and turn Wi-Fi off.

checks.title: YouTube ingest reachable
checks.detail: TCP connect p95 per ingest (port 1935): YouTube ingest (nearest) 66 ms.

checks.title: Twitch ingest reachable
checks.detail: TCP connect p95 per ingest (port 1935): Twitch ingest Seoul 39 ms, Twitch ingest Tokyo 87 ms. Reachability only - Twitch closed its Korean business in Feb 2024; do a 30-second test stream with the real key from this venue.

checks.title: Wired network connection
checks.detail: No wired network adapter is connected. Wi-Fi cannot carry 2x 1080p60 OMT/NDI reliably. Adapters up: vEthernet (WSL (Hyper-V firewall)) [virtual], vEthernet (Default Switch) [virtual], WiFi [wifi].
checks.fix: Connect the PC to the production switch with an Ethernet cable (2.5 GbE or faster) for the NDI/OMT feeds.

checks.title: LAN headroom for incoming feeds
checks.detail: No wired adapter is up, so there is no usable path for the incoming feeds.
checks.fix: Connect a wired Ethernet adapter first.

checks.title: Virtual network adapters
checks.detail: NDI/OMT discovery may bind to vEthernet (WSL (Hyper-V firewall)), vEthernet (Default Switch).
checks.fix: Disable the virtual adapters for the show, or pin the adapter in NDI Access Manager / vMix.

checks.title: Windows network profile
checks.detail: No wired adapter is up.

checks.title: Energy-Efficient Ethernet
checks.detail: No wired adapter is up.

checks.title: CPU threads
checks.detail: 13th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i5-1340P - low-power laptop CPU (12 cores)

checks.title: RAM
checks.detail: Installed RAM reads a few percent below its nominal size, so 32 GB is matched from 30.4 GB.
checks.fix: Install at least 32 GB of RAM (64 GB is comfortable for vMix with 2 feeds).

checks.title: Dedicated GPU
checks.detail: Found: Intel(R) UHD Graphics; no dedicated GPU - vMix at 1080p60 with 3 encodes is not supported on integrated graphics. OBS alone may cope at lower settings, but expect dropped frames.
checks.fix: Use a PC with an NVIDIA RTX or AMD Radeon GPU for the show.

checks.title: NVENC encode sessions
checks.detail: No NVIDIA GPU: the NVENC session limit does not apply.

checks.title: Power plan and mains power
checks.detail: The Balanced plan lets the CPU slow down under bursty load, which shows up as dropped frames.
checks.fix: Set the Windows power plan to High performance (Control Panel > Power Options) and set sleep to Never.

checks.title: GPU driver age
checks.detail: No dedicated GPU.

checks.title: System drive free space
checks.detail: System drive C:.

checks.title: Pending Windows reboot
checks.detail: Windows is waiting for a restart (updates or driver install).
checks.fix: Reboot before the show, not during it.

checks.title: Hardware video encoder
checks.detail: The test encoded with h264_qsv. Encoders that did not work: h264_nvenc, h264_amf.

checks.title: Real-time 2 in + 3 out
checks.detail: Too slow for real time: out-srt (0.95 x) [speed_min 0.95 < threshold 0.97].
checks.fix: This PC cannot decode 2 feeds and encode 3 outputs in real time: use a stronger PC, or reduce outputs and bitrates.

checks.title: CPU load during test
checks.detail: CPU p95 during the test; vMix/OBS compositing is not included. Peak 128 %.
checks.fix: The CPU is already busy before vMix/OBS compositing is added: use a faster CPU or lower the encoder load.

checks.title: GPU encoder load during test
checks.detail: GPU video-encode engine load (p95) while encoding the three outputs.

checks.title: CPU clock throttling
checks.detail: CPU performance went from 133 % at the start to 58 % at its lowest.
checks.fix: The CPU slowed down under load (heat or power limit): set High performance, clean/cool the PC, plug in power, and re-run.

checks.title: vMix or OBS installed
checks.detail: A production mixer is installed.

checks.title: NDI / OMT software
checks.value: NDI runtime not found, DistroAV not found, OMT not found
checks.detail: The show uses OMT; make sure the sending PCs and vMix/OBS support it.

checks.title: Background apps
checks.detail: These programs compete for CPU, GPU or network: chrome, msedge.

settings.label: SRT latency (both ends)
settings.why: ~4 x p95 RTT 259 ms = 1036 ms, rounded up to 1,050 ms. Haivision table minimum 800 ms (3 x for loss <= 1 %); raised to 4 x because the path is long-haul (RTT > 150 ms) and short probes miss rare bursts. SRT needs several round trips to resend lost packets; the 120-125 ms encoder default will drop video on this path.

settings.label: SRT bandwidth overhead
settings.why: Haivision rule: at least the table overhead (1 %) and never below 100 / 4 = 25 %.

settings.label: SRT video bitrate
settings.why: Constant bitrate keeps the SRT overhead calculation valid; a 2 s keyframe interval is what the partner decoder expects.

settings.label: SRT mode
settings.value: caller, packet size 1316, same latency on both ends (receiver latency wins if higher)
settings.why: The Seoul PC calls out to the partner in France; both sides must be set so the higher latency is not a surprise.

settings.label: Ingest servers
settings.why: The Twitch host is the one with the fastest TCP connect from this venue.

settings.label: Input protocol
settings.why: There is no wired link with enough capacity for the incoming feeds.

settings.label: Windows power plan
settings.value: High performance (or Ultimate), on mains power, sleep off
settings.why: The default Balanced plan lets the CPU clock drop under bursty live-video load.

settings.label: Video encoder
settings.value: Intel Quick Sync H.264 (h264_qsv), veryfast preset, CBR, keyframe 2 s - same for all three outputs
settings.why: Chosen by the load test (first hardware encoder that worked).

manual_checks.text: Confirm the French partner's receive latency matches the SRT latency above (the higher of the two ends wins).
Twitch from Korea: do a 30-second test stream with the real stream key from this venue before show day.
Re-run ShowReady at the same time of day as the show (evening congestion differs from daytime).
Run a 30-minute rehearsal with the real vMix/OBS scene and both real feeds; watch vMix/OBS dropped frames.
When the partner sends their SRT IP, run: Run-ShowReady.cmd -SrtHost <their IP>.

reasons: the path is long-haul (RTT > 150 ms) and short probes miss rare bursts
